definition: The disciplined handling of information resources so an organization can scan, interpret, decide, learn, and act.
why_it_matters: AI agents are only useful when the underlying information environment has trusted sources, clear meaning, and operating rules.
business_use: Use it to diagnose where a business firm loses time, trust, or decision quality because information is fragmented.
source_references: By Sanchez Tacit vs Explicit Knowledge.pdf (page 17)
By Sanchez Tacit vs Explicit Knowledge.pdf (page 2)

definition: A view of information work as a human, organizational, process, and technology ecosystem rather than a technology-only problem.
why_it_matters: It keeps AI-agent projects from becoming narrow software installs disconnected from incentives and workflows.
business_use: Map people, processes, politics, data flows, tools, and decisions before designing an agent.
source_references: Department of Defense Zero Trust Reference Architecture.pdf (page 68)
Department of Defense Zero Trust Reference Architecture.pdf (page 91)

definition: The systematic collection and interpretation of external signals that affect strategy and operations.
why_it_matters: Business firms depend on market, tenant, lender, regulatory, and competitor signals.
business_use: Design market-intelligence agents that collect and summarize listings, comps, permits, rent trends, and policy changes.

definition: Know-how embedded in experience, judgment, context, and practice that is hard to write down completely.
why_it_matters: Many brokerage, leasing, maintenance, and asset-management decisions rely on expert judgment not captured in systems.
business_use: Interview top performers and convert patterns into playbooks, prompts, checklists, and review workflows.
source_references: By Sanchez Tacit vs Explicit Knowledge.pdf (page 6)
By Sanchez Tacit vs Explicit Knowledge.pdf (page 12)

definition: Knowledge that can be documented, stored, searched, taught, reused, and governed.
why_it_matters: AI agents need explicit procedures, source policies, and examples to act consistently.
business_use: Turn leasing SOPs, compliance rules, reporting standards, and objection handling into controlled knowledge assets.
source_references: By Sanchez Tacit vs Explicit Knowledge.pdf (page 6)
By Sanchez Tacit vs Explicit Knowledge.pdf (page 12)

definition: A representation of where critical knowledge lives, who owns it, how it flows, and where gaps exist.
why_it_matters: It reveals which workflows an AI agent can automate safely and which require human expertise capture first.
business_use: Build a knowledge map before automating maintenance triage, buyer lead routing, underwriting diligence, or investor reporting.

definition: A business-aligned plan for what data is needed, how it is governed, how it is used, and how it creates value.
why_it_matters: Without data strategy, agent projects drift into disconnected tools and unreliable outputs.
business_use: Use a data-strategy workshop to prioritize agent use cases by business value, data readiness, risk, and change effort.
source_references: The Chief Data Officer in Government_ A CDO Playbook3629.pdf (page 5)
How to create a data strategy.pdf (page 2)

definition: Decision rights, accountabilities, policies, standards, and controls for managing data as an asset.
why_it_matters: AI agents require clear ownership of sources, definitions, access, retention, and exception handling.
business_use: Create stewardship roles for CRM, property-management, lease, accounting, listing, and document data.
source_references: The Chief Data Officer in Government_ A CDO Playbook3629.pdf (page 6)

definition: An executive or senior role accountable for data strategy, governance, value creation, risk, and organizational enablement.
why_it_matters: Even small business firms need CDO-like responsibilities when deploying AI across sensitive workflows.
business_use: Translate CDO playbook ideas into fractional data-leadership services for clients without a formal CDO.
source_references: Department of Defense Zero Trust Reference Architecture.pdf (page 68)
The Chief Data Officer in Government_ A CDO Playbook8247.pdf (page 5)
The Chief Data Officer in Government_ A CDO Playbook8971.pdf (page 3)

definition: A big-data lens covering volume, velocity, variety, veracity, and value.
why_it_matters: It helps diagnose why a data or agent workflow is hard: too much data, too fast, too diverse, too untrusted, or not valuable.
business_use: Assess CRM notes, listing feeds, lease docs, maintenance tickets, emails, and financial reports before automation.

definition: Information that does not fit neatly into fixed tables, such as PDFs, emails, notes, contracts, photos, and call transcripts.
why_it_matters: Business firms have large stores of unstructured data where AI agents can create value if governance is strong.
business_use: Create document-intelligence agents for leases, diligence rooms, email triage, work orders, and investor updates.

definition: Creating measurable value from data through internal improvement, external products, partnerships, or revenue models.
why_it_matters: The best agent opportunities often monetize data indirectly through faster decisions, lower leakage, or better client service.
business_use: Frame AI-agent ROI around saved labor, higher conversion, lower vacancy, better diligence, faster reporting, and risk reduction.

definition: A reusable, governed data asset or service designed around a user need, quality contract, and value outcome.
why_it_matters: Agents should consume stable data products rather than improvised spreadsheet exports.
business_use: Create data products for property profiles, tenant history, lead status, deal pipeline, lease abstracts, or investor KPIs.
source_references: Department of Defense Zero Trust Reference Architecture.pdf (page 68)

definition: Policies, practices, and controls that protect personal or sensitive data across collection, use, sharing, retention, and deletion.
why_it_matters: Business workflows contain tenant, buyer, seller, employee, investor, and financial data.
business_use: Define privacy requirements before connecting AI agents to CRM, email, documents, accounting, or property systems.

definition: A security model that assumes no implicit trust and continuously verifies identities, devices, access, and activity.
why_it_matters: AI agents expand access paths into business systems, so least privilege and continuous verification become essential.
business_use: Design agent permissions around scoped roles, source-specific access, audit logs, approval gates, and revocation.

definition: A structured way to identify, protect, detect, respond, and recover from cybersecurity risks.
why_it_matters: Client-facing AI systems need operational resilience and incident readiness.
business_use: Use framework categories to scope agent security requirements, monitoring, vendor risk, and response procedures.
source_references: Department of Defense Zero Trust Reference Architecture.pdf (page 104)
HBR - A Guide to Building a More Resilient Business.pdf (page 3)

definition: A breakdown in moving relevant information to the people or systems that need it at the right time and context.
why_it_matters: Many business service failures are not knowledge absence; they are routing, trust, incentive, or context failures.
business_use: Design agents that route the right maintenance, leasing, compliance, or diligence context to the right reviewer.

definition: The degree to which a workflow has clear goals, trusted data, documented decisions, safe access, human oversight, and measurable ROI.
why_it_matters: It prevents selling automation into workflows that are not ready for reliable agent behavior.
business_use: Score each candidate workflow before implementation and choose the first pilot by readiness plus value.
